To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
H-Lu preconditioners are a viable alternative to direct solvers and multigrid preconditioners for sparse matrices.

• the hierarchical LU factorization (H-LU) of a dense matrix scales linearly in the size of the problem (i.e., in the number of unknowns) for a large class of sparse problems, • H-LU is faster than direct methods (such as the sparse Cholesky factorization) for a large number of sparse problems, including many from computational electromagnetism,
hierarchical matrices can be applied to large-scale problems in a black-box way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a black-box solver for large linear systems which scales close to linear in the matrix size and is competitive with state of the art solvers.
the development of fast solvers for large-scale linear systems.
the numerical solution of partial differential equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the H-matrix technique is competitive in the medium-scale case and superior in the large-scale case.
hierarchical matrices are a viable alternative to direct solvers for large-scale problems.
the performance of the H-matrices scales linearly in the size of the matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the H-LU preconditioning for sparse matrices is a very efficient and robust technique for the solution of large linear systems.
H-LU preconditioning is a very powerful technique, which can be applied to a wide class of problems and which can be used as a drop-in replacement for direct solvers.
H-LU is competitive with algebraic multigrid, but that the latter is still superior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H-matrices can be applied as a drop-in replacement for existing black-box solvers and yield speed-ups of up to 2 orders of magnitude.
the hierarchical matrix approach is able to solve problems of size O(106) in a time which is only a factor of two to three slower than the direct solvers.
H-matrices provide an efficient way to solve linear systems with matrices that are too large to fit into main memory, or for which the cost of direct methods becomes prohibitive.
